mainTopic: Doubtful תרומה and יש אם למקרא; שמואל's ruling like רבי שמעון on letting blood from a בכור; and the penalty for one who blemishes a בכור
overview: This amud opens at the end of a ברייתא about a בכור. It learns from the words 'כל מום' that one may not cause a blemish even indirectly, for example by putting food on the animal's ear so a dog will bite it. The גמרא then says that רבי אליעזר and רבי יהושע, who argue about guarding תרומה of uncertain purity, also argue about a פסוק: 'משמרת תרומתי'. At first it explains that רבי אליעזר follows the plural reading aloud, while רבי יהושע follows the singular spelling. This is challenged from the case of the אמה עבריה. There, רבי אליעזר learns 'בבגדו בה' from the spelling, not the reading. So the גמרא gives a new explanation: both learn that one must guard only תרומה 'fit for you'. רבי אליעזר holds that doubtful תרומה still counts as fit, because אליהו may come and declare it pure. Next, שמואל rules like רבי שמעון on letting blood from a בכור. The גמרא shows he means the רבי שמעון of the ברייתא, since his ruling on דבר שאין מתכוין is already known. Finally, a new משנה teaches that one who slits the ear of a בכור may never slaughter it, according to רבי אליעזר. The גמרא begins to challenge this from a משנה about a בהרת, and the challenge continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Even an indirect blemish is forbidden
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא finishes its teaching. The words 'כל מום' (any blemish) forbid causing a blemish even indirectly, such as putting food on the animal's ear so a dog will bite it.
steps.simpleTranslation: I would only know that a person may not directly put a blemish on the animal. How do we know he may not bring a pressed fig or dough and put it on the animal's ear, so that a dog will come and eat it (and bite the ear)? The פסוק says 'כל מום' — any blemish. This means both a direct blemish and any blemish at all.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא is finishing a teaching about causing a blemish to a sacred animal. It shows that even setting up an indirect blemish is forbidden.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Without the extra word, we would only forbid a person from making the blemish with his own hands. The extra word 'כל' widens the rule to include causing it indirectly through a dog. So this ברייתא forbids גרמא (indirect causing) on a בכור, and it learns this straight from a פסוק.

keyTerms.meaning: A blemish that disqualifies an animal from being a קרבן
'The verse teaches' — introduces the source in the פסוק
'Any blemish' — the extra word that widens the rule

steps.confusionAlert: This amud begins in the middle of a sentence. 'אלא שלא יתן בו מום' continues an earlier 'אין לי' ('I would only know'). It is not a full sentence by itself.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows that the people arguing in this case base their view on how to read a פסוק. The גמרא now says the same is true in the תרומה case.

phrases.english: [I would know] only that one may not put a blemish on it,
phrases.notes: Continues the words 'אין לי' from the previous part of the ברייתא.

phrases.english: from where [do we know] that one may not bring
a pressed fig or dough
and place it on the [animal's] ear
so that a dog will come and eat it?
phrases.notes: The dog would bite off part of the ear, leaving a blemish.

phrases.english: The verse teaches: 'any blemish' —
both a [direct] blemish and any blemish [even indirect].

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Ends the ברייתא about a בכור that started on the previous amud.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: It is forbidden to cause a blemish to a sacred animal even indirectly, learned from 'כל מום'.

steps.title: In the תרומה case too, the argument is about a פסוק
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא says the argument about doubtful תרומה is also about reading a פסוק. It brings the פסוק 'משמרת תרומתי', in the name of several אמוראים.
steps.simpleTranslation: Here too they argue about how to read the פסוקים. As רב יהודה said in the name of שמואל, and so said ריש לקיש, and so said רב נחמן in the name of רבה בר אבוה: 'And I, behold, I have given you the charge of My תרומות.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to the תרומה case. It says the תנאים there are also arguing about a פסוק, and it quotes that פסוק. This is setting up the next two steps, which explain each side.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Just as the תנאים of the בכור ברייתא argue about how to expound a פסוק, the גמרא now says the תנאים of the doubtful תרומה case also argue about a פסוק. The key word is 'תרומתי', which is read as plural but spelled in a way that can mean singular.

keyTerms.meaning: They argue about [how to read] פסוקים
And likewise said — adds more אמוראים who say the same thing

steps.whyThisMatters: The whole argument now depends on one word in the פסוק. This sets up the later question about יש אם למקרא.

phrases.english: Here [too] they disagree about verses,
as Rav Yehuda said that Shmuel said,
and so said Reish Lakish,

phrases.aramaic: וְכֵן אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר אֲבוּהּ:
phrases.english: and so said Rav Naḥman that Rabba bar Avuh said:
'And I, behold, I have given you
the charge of My terumot.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Just as the בכור ברייתא was based on a פסוק, the תרומה argument is also based on a פסוק.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The argument of רבי אליעזר and רבי יהושע about doubtful תרומה depends on how to read 'משמרת תרומתי'.

steps.title: רבי אליעזר: the plural means even doubtful תרומה must be guarded
steps.stepSummary: רבי אליעזר reads 'תרומתי' as plural, meaning two kinds of תרומה. Both pure תרומה and doubtful תרומה must be guarded.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אליעזר holds: the פסוק is talking about two kinds of תרומה. One is pure תרומה, and the other is תרומה תלויה (whose purity is uncertain). And the Torah says: guard it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains רבי אליעזר's side. He learns from the plural reading that even doubtful תרומה needs to be protected.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word is read aloud as 'תְּרוּמֹתַי', which is plural. Plural means more than one kind of תרומה, so doubtful תרומה is included too. That is why רבי אליעזר says you may not make it impure yourself.

phrases.english: Rabbi Eliezer holds:
the verse speaks of two terumot,
one, pure teruma,
and one, teruma in doubt,
and the Merciful One said: make a guarding for it.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר סָבַר: בִּשְׁתֵּי תְּרוּמוֹת הַכָּתוּב מְדַבֵּר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains how רבי אליעזר reads the פסוק just quoted.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Because the word is read as plural, even תרומה תלויה must be guarded.

steps.title: רבי יהושע: the spelling is singular
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהושע goes by the spelling 'תרומתי', which is singular. So only clearly pure תרומה must be guarded.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי יהושע: it is written 'תרומתי' (singular — My תרומה).
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives רבי יהושע's side. He follows how the word is spelled, not how it is read aloud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word is spelled without the extra letter for the plural, so it can be read as one תרומה. One kind means only definitely pure תרומה. So there is no duty to guard doubtful תרומה, and one may let it become impure.

keyTerms.meaning: It is written — referring to the spelling in the Torah
My תרומה (singular, based on the spelling)

steps.whatToRemember: רבי אליעזר learns from the plural reading, so doubtful תרומה must be guarded. רבי יהושע learns from the singular spelling, so only pure תרומה must be guarded.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yehoshua [holds]:
'My teruma' [singular] is written.
phrases.notes: The spelling is missing the letter ו that would show a plural.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the opposite reading to רבי אליעזר's.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Because the word is spelled as singular, only definitely pure תרומה must be guarded.

steps.title: Does רבי אליעזר follow the way a word is read aloud?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whether this means רבי אליעזר holds יש אם למקרא, that we learn from how a word is pronounced.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is this to say that רבי אליעזר holds יש אם למקרא (we follow the reading aloud)?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא draws a general rule from the last step and asks if it is really true. It is preparing to challenge it in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אליעזר learned from the pronounced plural and not from the singular spelling. That suggests he holds יש אם למקרא in general. The גמרא will now check this against another source.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Is this to say?' — the גמרא checks a conclusion it drew
The way a word is read aloud is the main source for learning

steps.confusionAlert: מקרא here means how a word is pronounced (the vowels). מסורת means how a word is spelled (the letters). Don't mix the two up.

phrases.english: Is this to say that Rabbi Eliezer holds
the reading [vocalization] is authoritative?

steps.triggerLanguage: לְמֵימְרָא דְּרַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר סָבַר יֵשׁ אֵם לַמִּקְרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws a general rule from רבי אליעזר's reading of the פסוק.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Does רבי אליעזר's reading show that he holds יש אם למקרא as a general rule?

steps.title: A contradiction from the case of the Hebrew maidservant
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a ברייתא to contradict this. It begins with רבי עקיבא's reading of 'בבגדו בה', based on how the word is read aloud. רבי אליעזר's opposite view comes next.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the גמרא raises a contradiction: 'בבגדו בה' — once he has spread his garment over her, he may no longer sell her. These are the words of רבי עקיבא.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts quoting a ברייתא that seems to contradict the idea that רבי אליעזר holds יש אם למקרא. This step only gives רבי עקיבא's opinion; the part that challenges רבי אליעזר comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word is read aloud as 'בְּבִגְדוֹ', and רבי עקיבא connects it to 'בִּגְדוֹ', 'his garment', so he follows the reading aloud (יש אם למקרא). He learns that once the master has spread his garment over her (taken her as a wife), her father may not sell her again. Later in the ברייתא, רבי אליעזר explains the word by its spelling, which would clash with how we explained his view on 'תרומתי'.

keyTerms.meaning: 'And they contrasted it' — the גמרא brings a source that seems to contradict
'In his dealing falsely with her' — also read as 'with his garment'

steps.confusionAlert: The contradiction is not finished yet. רבי עקיבא's opinion is only the start of the ברייתא. The clash with רבי אליעזר comes from his own view, which appears next.

phrases.english: And they raised a contradiction:
'seeing that he has dealt deceitfully with her [bevigdo bah]' —
phrases.notes: שמות כא:ח; the word is related to בגד, a garment.

phrases.english: once he has spread his cloak over her,
phrases.notes: This means he designated her as his wife.

phrases.english: he [the father] may no longer sell her,
[these are] the words of Rabbi Akiva.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a source to test the conclusion that רבי אליעזר holds יש אם למקרא.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that רבי אליעזר holds יש אם למקרא.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: In the ברייתא about אמה עבריה, רבי עקיבא follows the reading aloud. רבי אליעזר's opposing view (next passage) seems to follow the spelling, which contradicts how he read 'תרומתי'.

steps.title: רבי אליעזר follows the spelling in 'בבגדו בה'
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא ends with רבי אליעזר's view. He reads 'בבגדו' by its spelling and learns that a father who sold his daughter once may not sell her again. This finishes the contradiction.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אליעזר says: since the father acted unfairly with her, he may not sell her again!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes the challenge it started in the last step. Here רבי אליעזר learns from the written spelling of the word, not from how it is said aloud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'בבגדו' is spelled without a יו״ד, so it can be read 'בְּבָגְדוֹ', meaning 'in his acting unfairly'. That is how רבי אליעזר learns the father cannot sell her again. So here רבי אליעזר goes by spelling, which is the opposite of what we said he did with 'תרומתי'.

keyTerms.meaning: the written spelling of a פסוק is the main source for learning

steps.confusionAlert: Watch the switch. In 'תרומתי' we said רבי אליעזר goes by the reading aloud. Here he goes by the spelling. That clash is the whole point of the קשיא.

phrases.english: Rabbi Eliezer says:
since he acted unfairly with her,
he is no longer allowed to sell her!

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר אוֹמֵר: כֵּיוָן שֶׁבָּגַד בָּהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the ברייתא quoted in step 6 by giving רבי אליעזר's opposite reading.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim in step 5 that רבי אליעזר holds יש אם למקרא (we learn from how a word is read aloud).
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: In 'בבגדו בה' רבי אליעזר learns from the spelling, so he holds יש אם למסורת. That contradicts explaining his תרומה view through the reading aloud.

steps.title: A new reason for the doubtful תרומה dispute
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא drops the spelling-versus-reading explanation. Both sides agree on reading 'לך' (for you) as 'what is fit for you'. They argue about whether doubtful תרומה counts as fit.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, this is what they argue about. רבי יהושע holds: guard what is fit for you, and do not guard what is not fit for you. רבי אליעזר holds: this doubtful תרומה is also fit, because maybe אליהו will come and declare it pure.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the contradiction by giving a completely new reason for the תרומה argument. It is not about spelling or reading at all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק says 'I have given you (לך) the guarding of My תרומות'. Both sides learn that you must guard only תרומה that is 'fit for you'. רבי יהושע says doubtful תרומה cannot be eaten now, so it is not fit and need not be guarded. רבי אליעזר says it is still fit, because אליהו might one day clear up the doubt and declare it pure.

keyTerms.meaning: rather, we drop the earlier explanation
Elijah the prophet, who will settle doubts in the future

steps.whatToRemember: Final explanation of the תרומה argument: both sides agree on reading 'לך'. They argue whether doubtful תרומה counts as 'fit for you'. רבי אליעזר says yes, because אליהו may come and make it pure.
steps.whyThisMatters: Because of this answer, רבי אליעזר no longer contradicts himself. His view about spelling can stay as it is in 'בבגדו בה'.

phrases.english: Rather, here they argue about this:
Rabbi Yehoshua holds:
what is fit for you, guard;
phrases.notes: Learned from the word 'לך' in the פסוק.

phrases.english: and what is not fit for you, do not guard;
and Rabbi Eliezer holds:
this one is also fit,
since perhaps Elijah will come and declare it pure.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the contradiction from step 7 by replacing the earlier explanation.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Replaces the reason behind the dispute (אלא): a new basis for the argument.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We first thought they argue about spelling versus reading of 'תרומתי'.
steps.terutzMaskana: They argue about whether doubtful תרומה is 'fit for you', since אליהו might make it pure.

steps.title: שמואל rules like רבי שמעון
steps.stepSummary: A new section starts. רב יהודה quotes שמואל: the הלכה follows רבי שמעון. This is about our משנה on letting blood from a בכור.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said in the name of שמואל: the הלכה follows רבי שמעון.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to our משנה about letting blood from a בכור and gives a ruling. This short line sets up the question that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the משנה, רבי שמעון allows letting blood from a sick בכור even if it causes a blemish. A blemish is a problem for a בכור, but the goal here is only to heal it. שמואל's ruling seems to back that view, but the next step questions what he really meant.

keyTerms.meaning: the final ruling follows this opinion

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said that Shmuel said:
The halakha is like Rabbi Shimon.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל: הֲלָכָה כְּרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new topic. It returns to the משנה about letting blood from a בכור.

steps.title: Which רבי שמעון did שמואל mean?
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן בר יצחק asks which רבי שמעון שמואל meant. It cannot be the רבי שמעון of our משנה, because שמואל already taught that an unintended result is permitted.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן בר יצחק challenged this: which רבי שמעון? If you say the רבי שמעון of our משנה, hasn't שמואל already taught us that an unintended result is permitted?
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן בר יצחק attacks the ruling. He says it cannot be about our משנה, because then שמואל would be repeating himself.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי שמעון's view in the משנה rests on the rule of דבר שאין מתכוין. The person only wants to heal the animal, and the blemish is just a side effect he does not intend. שמואל already ruled like רבי שמעון on that general rule. So saying it again here would add nothing, and an אמורא does not repeat a ruling for no reason.

keyTerms.meaning: an allowed action that leads to a forbidden result the person did not intend

phrases.aramaic: מַתְקֵיף לַהּ רַב נַחְמָן בַּר יִצְחָק:
phrases.english: Rav Naḥman bar Yitzḥak challenged it:
Which Rabbi Shimon?
If you say the Rabbi Shimon of our mishna,
until now hasn't Shmuel already taught us
that an unintended act is permitted?

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְקֵיף לַהּ רַב נַחְמָן בַּר יִצְחָק: הֵי רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן
steps.kashyaTarget: The idea that שמואל's ruling refers to רבי שמעון in our משנה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: שמואל already ruled that דבר שאין מתכוין is permitted, so ruling again here would be a pointless repeat.

steps.title: Proof that שמואל already ruled on unintended acts
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא backs up the challenge. Two different chains of transmission show that שמואל already ruled like רבי שמעון on דבר שאין מתכוין, while רב ruled like רבי יהודה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Didn't רבי חייא בר אשי say in the name of רב: the הלכה follows רבי יהודה? And רב חנין בר אשי said in the name of שמואל: the הלכה follows רבי שמעון. And רב חייא בר אבין teaches it without naming the men in between: רב said the הלכה follows רבי יהודה, and שמואל said the הלכה follows רבי שמעון!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא proves that the challenge is right: שמואל really did already rule on this question. This is part of רב נחמן בר יצחק's attack.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה forbids דבר שאין מתכוין, and רבי שמעון permits it. Two separate traditions report that רב follows רבי יהודה and שמואל follows רבי שמעון. So שמואל's general view is already well known, which makes the ruling in step 9 look like an unneeded repeat if it is about our משנה.

keyTerms.meaning: without naming the people in the chain of transmission

phrases.aramaic: וְהָא רַבִּי חִיָּיא בַּר אָשֵׁי אָמַר רַב:
phrases.english: But didn't Rabbi Ḥiyya bar Ashi say that Rav said:
The halakha is like Rabbi Yehuda,
phrases.notes: רבי יהודה forbids דבר שאין מתכוין.

phrases.aramaic: וְרַב חָנִין בַּר אָשֵׁי אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל:
phrases.english: and Rav Ḥanin bar Ashi said that Shmuel said:
The halakha is like Rabbi Shimon,
phrases.notes: רבי שמעון permits דבר שאין מתכוין.

phrases.aramaic: וְרַב חִיָּיא בַּר אָבִין מַתְנֵי בְּלָא גַּבְרֵי —
phrases.english: and Rav Ḥiyya bar Avin teaches it without the intermediate men:
Rav said: The halakha is like Rabbi Yehuda,
and Shmuel said: The halakha is like Rabbi Shimon!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָא רַבִּי חִיָּיא בַּר אָשֵׁי אָמַר רַב: הֲלָכָה כְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the challenge in step 10 by showing where שמואל's earlier ruling comes from.
steps.raayaObject: That שמואל already ruled that דבר שאין מתכוין is permitted.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The traditions of רבי חייא בר אשי, רב חנין בר אשי, and רב חייא בר אבין.

steps.title: שמואל meant רבי שמעון of the ברייתא
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers רב נחמן בר יצחק's challenge. שמואל was not ruling like the רבי שמעון of our משנה. He was ruling like the רבי שמעון of the ברייתא.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, שמואל meant the רבי שמעון of the ברייתא.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question from Step 10. שמואל's ruling refers to the רבי שמעון in the ברייתא, not the one in our משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If שמואל were ruling like the רבי שמעון of our משנה, his statement would add nothing. He already ruled like רבי שמעון on דבר שאין מתכוין. The רבי שמעון of the ברייתא says something new: one may let blood even though it makes a blemish, and one may even slaughter the animal because of that blemish. So שמואל's ruling teaches a new חידוש.

keyTerms.meaning: A teaching of the תנאים that was not included in the משנה
The תנא whose view שמואל adopts

steps.confusionAlert: There are two statements of רבי שמעון here: one in our משנה and one in the ברייתא. They are not the same. The one in the ברייתא goes further.

phrases.english: Rather, it is Rabbi Shimon of the baraita.
phrases.notes: This refers to the ברייתא on 33b.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge raised in Step 10 and backed up in Step 11.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Re-identifying the source of the ruling
steps.terutzHavaAmina: שמואל's ruling seemed to be about the רבי שמעון of our משנה, which would make it repetitive.
steps.terutzMaskana: שמואל's ruling is about the רבי שמעון of the ברייתא, so it teaches a new point.

steps.title: רב שישא teaches שמואל's ruling explicitly
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא supports the answer. רב שישא בריה דרב אידי taught שמואל's statement with the words 'the רבי שמעון of the ברייתא' spelled out openly.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רב שישא, son of רב אידי, teaches it explicitly: רב יהודה said in the name of שמואל: the הלכה follows the רבי שמעון of the ברייתא.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows that the answer it just gave is not a guess. Another version of the teaching says it outright.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the version that רב יהודה quoted in Step 9, it was unclear which רבי שמעון was meant. רב שישא's version names the ברייתא directly. This confirms the answer in Step 12.

keyTerms.meaning: He teaches it (a version of the teaching)

steps.whatToRemember: שמואל rules like the רבי שמעון of the ברייתא. One may let blood from a בכור even though this makes a blemish, and the blemish can then permit slaughtering it.

phrases.english: And Rav Sheisha, son of Rav Idi,
teaches it explicitly:
Rav Yehuda said that Shmuel said:
The halakha is like Rabbi Shimon of the baraita.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַב שִׁישָׁא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב אִידִי מַתְנֵי לַהּ בְּהֶדְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Confirms the answer of Step 12 with an explicit version of the teaching.
steps.raayaObject: The claim that שמואל meant the רבי שמעון of the ברייתא
steps.raayaSupportSource: רב שישא בריה דרב אידי's explicit version of שמואל's statement

steps.title: New משנה: one who slits the ear of a firstborn
steps.stepSummary: A new משנה begins. רבי אליעזר says that someone who slits the ear of a בכור may never slaughter it. The חכמים say that if another blemish develops, he may slaughter it because of that blemish.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: If someone slits the ear of a בכור, he may never slaughter it. This is רבי אליעזר's view. The חכמים say: if another blemish appears on it, he may slaughter it because of that blemish.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה starts. It deals with a person who deliberately blemishes a בכור, and with whether he may ever slaughter it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A בכור may only be slaughtered outside the מקדש once it has a blemish. Here the owner made the blemish himself on purpose, so he is penalized and may not use that blemish. רבי אליעזר makes the penalty permanent. The חכמים say a later blemish that comes on its own does permit slaughtering.

keyTerms.meaning: One who slits or nicks (the ear)
Firstborn animal, which is holy and given to a כהן

steps.confusionAlert: Both sides agree that the blemish he made himself cannot be used. They only argue about a second blemish that comes later on its own.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the source of the penalty (קנס) against someone who blemishes a בכור on purpose.

phrases.english: MISHNA:
One who slits the ear of a firstborn,
that person may never slaughter it,
these are the words of Rabbi Eliezer.
And the Rabbis say:

phrases.aramaic: נוֹלַד בּוֹ מוּם אַחֵר — יִשְׁחוֹט עָלָיו.
phrases.english: If another blemish develops in it, he may slaughter it on account of that blemish.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה and a new topic.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי אליעזר: someone who blemishes a בכור may never slaughter it. חכמים: a later blemish permits slaughtering it.

steps.title: Does רבי אליעזר really penalize forever?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whether רבי אליעזר really imposes a permanent penalty. It begins to quote a contradicting משנה about a person with a בהרת (a leprous mark).
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: Does רבי אליעזר really penalize forever? A contradiction was raised: one who had a בהרת...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבי אליעזר's view in our משנה. It starts quoting another משנה where he seems to hold differently.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Our משנה shows רבי אליעזר making a penalty last forever. The גמרא is about to bring a משנה in נגעים where רבי אליעזר seems not to penalize forever. The full contradiction continues on the next amud.

keyTerms.meaning: A bright white leprous mark (a type of נגע)

phrases.english: GEMARA:
But does Rabbi Eliezer penalize forever?
And they raised a contradiction:
One who had a bright leprous mark
phrases.notes: This begins the משנה in נגעים 7:5. It continues on the next amud.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמִי קָנֵיס רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר לְעוֹלָם? וּרְמִינְהִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבי אליעזר's ruling in the new משנה.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי אליעזר's view that the penalty lasts forever
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Another משנה about removing a בהרת seems to show that רבי אליעזר does not impose permanent penalties, so his view here seems contradictory.
